findings.title: Improper Validation of Link Protocols
findings.description: The `isAnchorLinkAllowed` function in `src/runtime/parser/utils/props.ts` attempts to sanitize URLs by checking for dangerous protocols, but the logic is brittle and can potentially be bypassed by whitespace or encoding tricks.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a markdown link with a protocol such as `javascript:alert(1)` using variations like `  javascript:` or encoded characters.
If the validation logic incorrectly flags the origin check, it may permit the dangerous link.
Users clicking the link trigger the JavaScript execution in their browser.
findings.impact: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via injected anchor tags.

findings.title: Improper Validation of Link Protocols
findings.description: The `isAnchorLinkAllowed` function attempts to sanitize URIs but may be bypassed by various encoding tricks or path manipulations, allowing restricted protocols.
steps_to_exploit: Use obfuscated URI schemes or complex URL structures not caught by the `new URL()` constructor.
The link is rendered as an `<a>` tag, allowing XSS upon user click.
findings.impact: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) when clicking malicious links.
